stories.summary: Meta's Superintelligence Labs released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Oct 12, the company's first frontier models. Mark Zuckerberg announced them on X, calling them state-of-the-art for personal and professional agentic work, with Active Memory (retains relevant user context across conversations) and Active Focus (persists through complex tasks, recovering from errors). Independent benchmarker Artificial Analysis scored Wonder Full at 56 on its Intelligence Index, above GPT-6 Astra's 53, and Meta shares rose about 3-4% on the announcement.
stories.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder frontier models with Active Memory and Active Focus

stories.summary: Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300, the third generation of its custom AI chip, and said it plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year as the primary inference system for Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Teams and agentic services. The chip uses a multi-chiplet design with TSMC 2nm compute chiplets, 288GB of HBM4 memory and 18TB/s of bandwidth; Microsoft claims about 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. CEO Satya Nadella called it 'our biggest bet yet on our own silicon' in an X post, with gigawatt-scale deployments starting in 2027.
stories.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 AI chip, plans million-chip 2027 deployment

stories.summary: Artificial-intelligence-related stocks sold off across Asia on Tuesday as investors grew concerned about the sustainability of the massive spending boom underpinning the AI trade, with rising bond yields and financing costs threatening the investment case for AI infrastructure. Nearly four years after ChatGPT launched, billions have flowed into semiconductor makers, data-center operators and related businesses, but signs of strain are emerging as investors question whether expected returns will justify the outlays.
stories.title: AI trade faces biggest test yet as chip stocks tumble across Asia

stories.source: Yellow / DBS Asia Future Forward Conference
stories.summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said Monday in Singapore that capital, not wafer or memory shortages, may become the biggest constraint on AI growth, and that demand for compute could outrun supply through 2029 and possibly into 2030. Tan noted Broadcom is working through supply bottlenecks and said frontier labs Anthropic and OpenAI are already generating significant revenue from the latest models deployed as AI personal assistants.
stories.title: Broadcom CEO: cash, not chips, is AI's biggest hurdle with demand into 2030
